Applicant has filed this second bail application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 in connection with Crime No. 689/2021 registered at P.S - Gandhwani, District- Dhar (M.P.) for commission of offence punishable under Sections 366, 376(2)(n), 376(2)(k), 344,
450, 294, 323, 506 of IPC.
As per prosecution story, on 25/09/2021 at about 8.00 pm, when the prosecutrix went to shop, at that time, the applicant met her and told that he loves her and wants to marry with her.

Thereafter,
on the pretext of marriage, the applicant abducted the prosecutrix and took her with him at Gujrat,
where he kept her in a hut and repeatedly committed rape upon her.

sentences.text: Accordingly, the aforementioned offence has been registered against the applicant.
Learned counsel for the applicant contended that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in this offence.
There is no legal evidence available on record to connect the applicant with the aforementioned offence.
Investigation is over and charge-sheet has been filed.
Prosecutrix (PW-1) has been examined before the trial Court and she has turned hostile and did not state anything against the applicant in respect of the aforementioned offence.
Applicant is in custody since 10/12/2021.
Final conclusion of trial shall take sufficient long time.
Under the above circumstances, prayer for grant of bail may be considered on such terms and conditions, as this Court deems fit and proper.
Per-contra, learned PL for respondent - State opposes the bail application and prays for its rejection.
Learned counsel for the objector submitted that the matter has been amicably settled between both the parties and the prosecutrix has no objection, if bail is granted to the applicant.
Perused the impugned order of the trial Court as well as the case dairy.

Considering all the facts and circumstances of the case, arguments advanced by both the parties,
nature of allegation as also taking note of the fact that prosecutrix (PW-1) has been examined before the trial Court and she has turned hostile; she categorically stated in her statement that present applicant neither abducted, nor committed rape upon her; the prosecutrix has no objection for grant of bail to the applicant; in view of the evidence available on record, I deem it proper to release the accused / applicant on bail.
Accordingly, without commenting on the merits of the case, the application is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant be released on bail on his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs. 75,000/-
(Rs. Seventy Five Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his appearance before the trial Court, as and when required.
He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated u/S. 437(3) Cr.P.C., Certified copy, as per Rules.

(ANIL VERMA) JUDGE amol Rahul vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43305613/
